transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Tara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Connor Blake (Redwood SE), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (BlueHarbor), Samir Gupta (BlueHarbor), Evan Ross (BlueHarbor), Olivia Chen (BlueHarbor)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Goal: scope POC that validates privacy controls + performance for BlueHarbor's conversational assistant.
- Success criteria discussed: redaction accuracy, retention policy enforcement, latency < 250ms 95p for short prompts, throughput 50 req/s for peak query patterns, and no sensitive data persisted beyond retention window.
- Next steps: share security docs, exchange sample workload, schedule baseline benchmark.

Topics: PII handling, prompt storage, logging & redaction flows, retention TTLs, benchmark sizing, timeline & gating criteria.

[00:00] Tara: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is tara from redwood, i'm the AE on this, and with me is connor our se, and luis is on as backup. how are you all?
[00:10] Maya: good, thanks. excited to map this out. i'll be running point on privacy.
[00:15] Samir: hey team, samir — platform lead. main thing is we need a clear path for sensitive fields to never land in long term storage.
[00:22] Connor: great. quick agenda, we'll run through our understanding of the use case, go over data handling patterns (what you want redacted vs what can be logged), then sizing and bench approach, and finish with timelines. sound good?
[00:32] Olivia: yep. also curious about prompt storage — how much of the raw prompt gets stored, can we truncate?

[00:40] Tara: perfect. so quick context from our side: redwood supports hosted and private deployments, with options for prompt redaction, on-the-fly redaction, and configurable retention TTLs. but we'll tailor the POC to your compliance constraints.
[00:52] Maya: to be explicit, blueharbor cannot retain full account numbers, tax ids, or full ssns, even in logs. hashed tokens are okay if irreversible. also need audit trails for who accessed the data.
[01:05] Connor: understood. for POCs we typically model three tiers: 1) no prompt storage (ephemeral only for inference), 2) truncated prompt storage (for debugging/observability), and 3) full prompt storage with encryption and KMS. we can show tradeoffs in the bench.
[01:20] Samir: what's the perf delta usually between ephemeral-only and full prompt retention?
[01:25] Connor: roughly, ephemeral-only can be slightly faster because there's no write to persistence, but the dominant cost is the tokenization + model latency. when you add synchronous logging to a durable store that adds, say, 20–80ms depending on your pipeline and region. but we have async logging modes.
[01:40] Evan: so async logging would ensure we don't block inference for logs? any risk of losing logs?
[01:46] Connor: yes async decouples writes — we can ack requests to the client before logs are flushed. there is a small risk window if a node crashes before flush, but we can combine with durable S3-like storage and retries to reduce that to near zero. tomography.* (transcription artifact)
[01:58] Maya: can you do automatic redaction on the model output and on logs? we need both.
[02:04] Connor: yes, we've got two layers. pre- and post-processing rules: pre-processing strips or masks tokens in the prompt before it's sent to the model; post-processing scans the model output and removes any detected PII. for logs we can run the redaction step before persisting. note: detection isn't perfect so we'll want a test set you provide.
[02:22] Olivia: about detection: will that be regex only or ML-based entity detection?
[02:28] Connor: we support both. regex for structured things like account numbers, and an NER model for names, addresses — we can tune thresholds. we'll include examples in the benchmark.
[02:36] Samir: for the POC can we run a sim of production peak: ~50 req/s sustained for 15 minutes, with spikes to 150 req/s? that's our target for the assistant.
[02:45] Tara: yes that's reasonable. our dedicated pools or hosted with burst capacity can hit that. we'll size the GPU cluster for model variant you pick; for example a 7B quantized variant can do X tokens/s, larger models need more GPUs. we'll capture that in the benchmark matrix.
[02:58] Maya: success criteria reminders: 1) no PII in persisted logs, 2) redaction false negative rate < 0.5% on your sample set, 3) latency SLO 95th < 250ms for prompts < 120 tokens, and 4) throughput 50 req/s sustained. are we aligned?
[03:15] Tara: that's perfect. we'll formalize, but those are reasonable gating criteria.

[03:30] (walkthrough of proposed bench matrix)
[03:30] Connor: so here's the proposed benchmark matrix — we'll test three model profiles (fast-quantized small, standard-llama-like medium, and safety-checked larger), three logging configs (ephemeral, truncated, full-encrypted), and two redaction modes (regex-only, regex+ner). measurements: median latency, p95 latency, error rate, redaction FN/FPR, and token cost.
[03:55] Samir: sounds good. how will you simulate user prompt shapes? we have multiple templates: short accounting queries (avg 40 tokens), long policy clarifications (avg 220 tokens), and multi-turn flows.
[04:10] Connor: please share a small sample set with anonymized fields — we can replay them with preserved token lengths. important to keep the same tokenization shape.
[04:22] Maya: we'll generate a 200-record sample including negatives — intentionally messy redaction cases.
[04:28] Tara: perfect. one note on prompt storage: we can support configurable TTLs per-org and per-route. e.g., route /payments can have 7-day TTL and be encrypted with the customer KMS; routes with highly sensitive info can be set to zero retention.
[04:45] Evan: on KMS — can we bring our own key? HSM?
[04:50] Connor: yes BYOK is supported in Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have a customer-managed key integration option across major cloud KMS providers. for HSM-level requirements we'll need a private deployment or dedicated offering.
[05:03] Olivia: audit logs — can you provide per-token billing-level logs or just per-request? we need enough fidelity for forensics.
[05:11] Tara: console provides token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing. for PII audits we can configure redaction-safe traces that show metadata (token counts, durations) without the raw prompt.
[05:24] Samir: curious about false positives with redaction. we don't want to remove necessary context. do you support a dual-path where redacted content can be reviewed in a secure vault?
[05:33] Connor: yes we can route redacted items to a secure review bucket that's KMS encrypted and accessible via strict RBAC. reviewers can see original content only if they have permissions. that's often used in finance.
[05:42] Maya: ok good. that helps incident investigations.

[05:50] (timing and timeline discussion)
[05:50] Tara: timeline proposal: week 1 — exchange security docs + sample dataset; week 2 — Redwood runs baseline bench in staging and shares results; week 3 — iterate on redaction rules and run targeted bench; week 4 — joint review and decision. does that fit your procurement and legal windows?
[06:10] Samir: legal will need two weeks to review contracts; procurement requires an internal approval cycle. the POC timeline is ok as long as deliverables map.
[06:19] Evan: we'll need an MOU or POC addendum clarifying data handling responsibilities.
[06:24] Tara: we have a POC addendum template — i'll send it. note that any private deployment requests will need a separate SOW.
[06:33] Maya: can you run the bench with our identity tokens obfuscated to check for any leakage? we want to ensure model completions never re-surface PII.
[06:41] Connor: yes, we'll include a leakage test in the bench — prompt injection and regurgitation tests. we'll also run an N-gram overlap check between input and output to detect verbatim copies.
[06:52] Olivia: what about retention enforcement — is that policy-driven or manual removal?
[06:58] Connor: policy-driven TTL enforcement. you can set per-route TTLs and we enforce automatic deletion; we also provide purge APIs for immediate removal.
[07:07] Samir: for the benchmark nodes where you log, will logging affect latency heavily? we might accept a small latency add for richer logs.
[07:15] Connor: yes we can measure both synchronous logging (adds latency) and async (minimal impact). we'll run both to show the tradeoffs.

[07:30] (technical deep-dive begins — Connor leads)
[07:30] Connor: on the runtime side we'll leverage KV cache for multi-turn to speed up repeated context. note: KV cache is memory-resident and not persisted; that'll help latency but not affect retention policy. also we can evict or scrub the cache on session end.
[07:45] Maya: good to know. cache eviction must be guaranteed for sessions flagged as sensitive.
[07:50] Connor: we can attach sensitivity tags to routes so the runtime triggers immediate cache scrub on completion.
[07:57] Samir: for throughput — are you using batching? how do you balance batching and latency?
[08:02] Connor: yes continuous batching with adaptive thresholds. you configure a max wait (e.g., 5–15ms) and target batch sizes. for latency-sensitive routes we use smaller max wait. our optimize tooling can recommend settings based on your observed tail latencies.
[08:18] Olivia: will you provide a runbook if we need to raise the concurrency?
[08:21] Tara: yes, we'll provide an ops runbook and suggested autoscaling policy for Dedicated. for hosted we'll propose burst config.

[08:35] (questions from BlueHarbor)
[08:35] Maya: quick one — retention proof: can you show that deleted prompts are unrecoverable?
[08:41] Connor: for hosted we can show deletion logs and ensure no backups contain the data; for private/dedicated we can provide stronger attestations and proof-of-deletion scripts you can run in your environment.
[08:52] Evan: what about third-party vendor risk — any subprocessors?
[08:56] Tara: we'll share the subprocessors list in the security pack. commonly used cloud infra and monitoring vendors are listed; we support DPA addenda.

[09:05] (recap and explicit next steps)
[09:05] Tara: ok recap: we have success criteria — redaction FN < 0.5%, latency p95 < 250ms for short prompts, throughput 50 req/s. action items — tara sends security pack and poc addendum; connor builds benchmark matrix and suggested infra config; samir/maya upload sample dataset; schedule bench window for week of 2026-03-09.
[09:30] Maya: agreed. please include the redaction review vault flow and RBAC examples.
[09:36] Tara: will do. i'll also add a BYOK note for kms options.
[09:40] Samir: procurement note — can we get an estimate for dedicated pricing if we exceed hosted burst? we might want to cost it out.
[09:47] Tara: yes i'll include a rough cost estimate for the dedicated pool sized for the benchmark.

[09:55] (wrap-up)
[09:55] Olivia: thanks all. this was super useful.
[09:58] Tara: thank you. we'll follow up with the docs in 24–48 hours.
[10:00] Meeting ends.

Appendix — rough benchmark plan (short):
- Baseline: 10k requests replay across 3 prompt shapes; measure latency median/p95/p99, errors, and redaction FN rate.
- Load test: sustained 50 req/s for 15 minutes, spike to 150 req/s for 60s (observe tail).
- Redaction tests: run synthetic PII injection cases and measure leakage and FN/FPR.
